issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require the Animal#getName() and Animal#setName(String) methods to have protected visibility (UML uses '#' and the text instructs protected getters/setters). The UML also indicates a protected Animal(String) constructor. However, the solution implementation declares the constructor and both accessor methods as public in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java. This mismatch between the specified (protected) visibility and the solution's public visibility can confuse students about the intended access level and inheritance design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor and the getName()/setName(...) methods protected to match the UML and problem text (or alternatively update the problem/UML to state public if that was intended). Concretely, change in Animal.java: 'public Animal(String name)' -> 'protected Animal(String name)', 'public String getName()' -> 'protected String getName()', and 'public void setName(String newName)' -> 'protected void setName(String newName)'.
